Validate a SAINT input list

Source: R/validate.R
validate_saint_input.Rd

Checks that si is valid input for run_saint(): if validate_saint_input() passes, run_saint() accepts the same si and mode. The checks are the ones listed in the section "Input tables" below, applied after the columns have been matched by name or position.

Usage

validate_saint_input(si, mode = c("spc", "int"))

Arguments

si

A named list with the data frames inter, prey and bait, in any order. See the section "Input tables".

mode

"spc" for spectral counts, "int" for intensities. Sets the allowed range of quant.

Value

TRUE invisibly on success; otherwise stops with a message naming the table and column at fault.

Input tables

Columns are matched by name when all required names are present; otherwise by position, in the order listed (as in the headerless native input files). A column that already carries a required name must then be at that name's position. Further columns are ignored.

inter, one row per prey detected in an IP (purification):

ColumnTypeContent
ipIdcharacterIP identifier, as in bait$ipId
baitIdcharacterBait of the IP, as in bait$baitId
preyIdcharacterPrey identifier, as in prey$preyId
quantnumericSpectral count, whole number >= 0 ("spc"), or intensity, > 0 ("int")

prey, one row per prey:

ColumnTypeContent
preyIdcharacterUnique prey identifier
preyLengthnumericProtein length (optional, not used in scoring)
preyGeneIdcharacterGene name, reported as PreyGene (optional, defaults to preyId)

The prey table is matched by name when it has both preyId and preyGeneId. Otherwise the first column is preyId; with two columns the second is preyLength if numeric, else preyGeneId; with three or more, the second is preyLength and the third preyGeneId.

bait, one row per IP:

ColumnTypeContent
ipIdcharacterUnique IP identifier
baitIdcharacterBait name; replicate IPs share it
CorTcharacter"T" for a test IP, "C" for a negative control

Every inter$ipId must be in bait, every inter$preyId in prey, each prey at most once per IP, and inter$baitId must agree with bait. At least one test and one control IP are needed.

Examples

si <- list(
  inter = data.frame(
    ipId = c("IP1", "IP2", "IP3"),
    baitId = c("BaitA", "BaitA", "Ctrl"),
    preyId = c("Prey1", "Prey1", "Prey1"),
    quant = c(12, 9, 1)
  ),
  prey = data.frame(preyId = "Prey1", preyLength = 500, preyGeneId = "GENE1"),
  bait = data.frame(
    ipId = c("IP1", "IP2", "IP3"),
    baitId = c("BaitA", "BaitA", "Ctrl"),
    CorT = c("T", "T", "C")
  )
)
validate_saint_input(si, mode = "spc")
